newsitem.title: CANADA: IBM Canada to sell unit to Onex.
newsitem.headline: IBM Canada to sell unit to Onex.

text.p: IBM Canada will sell its Celestica computer products and services company to Onex Corp. for about C$750 million ($550.6 million), the companies said Tuesday.

Celestica was established as a wholly owned unit of IBM Canada in January 1994. The company, which employs about 1,000 workers, produces memory products and power systems and provides contract manufacturing services for Canadian and international customers.
IBM Canada, a unit of International Business Machines Corp., said Celestica had reached a stage where independent ownership was the next logical step.
The companies said final agreements were expected in the next 60 days.
Onex Corp. is an investment company with interests in airline catering and auto parts.
"Celestica is an outstanding corporation and will be Onex's largest acquisition," Gerald Schwartz, Onex president and chief executive, said in a statement.
He said Celestica would continue to be based at its facilities in Toronto.
IBM's stock fell 75 cents to $123.75 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning.
